title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
why_read: A practical infrastructure contribution for testing and training AI agents that operate web browsers, addressing the real problem of unstable live websites.
analysis: WebHarbor is a set of 153 dockerized, self-contained copies of real websites built so that AI agents controlling a web browser can be tested and trained in stable, repeatable conditions. This matters because testing such agents against live websites is unreliable, since page content changes constantly and many useful workflows require logging in, which is hard to simulate safely at scale. The dataset includes thousands of multi-step tasks, including ones that require authentication, which prior benchmarks often lacked. The authors show a mid-sized open model trained with reinforcement learning in this environment performs competitively with existing open-source web agents, suggesting the environment is genuinely useful for training, not just evaluation.
